title: Recipient calls fake support who asks for card details vs. genuine support raises a ticket
summary: The recipient phones a "ShopKart customer care" number because the refund for a returned item has not arrived. In the fraud case, the number was taken from a web search result and belongs to an impostor, who says the refund must be "re-credited" to the card and asks for the full card number, expiry date, and CVV. In the legitimate case, the number is ShopKart's own; the agent checks the order, confirms the refund went to the card ending `[ACCT_LAST4]`, raises a ticket, and asks for nothing sensitive. Unlike most families, the recipient speaks first. Both agents mention the card, the refund, and "verification".

shared_setting.recipient_profile: a ShopKart customer who returned the item a week ago; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Source of the number (private, not emitted in the prefix): _F from a search-engine result; _L from the Help section of the ShopKart app. The recipient does not say where they found the number, so the source cannot act as a cue.
Both agents greet politely, give an agent name, and ask for the order number.

fraud.label_rationale: The agent asks for the full card number, expiry date, and CVV to "process" a refund. Refunds to a card need none of these from the customer, and no genuine entity asks for CVV.
fraud.caller_objective: Obtain card credentials (and a following OTP) to make a purchase or transfer.
stable_facts: The agent says the refund "bounced" and must be re-credited manually.
The agent says the details are needed "for verification" and the refund will arrive "within minutes".
The agent does not raise or quote any ticket number.

legitimate.label_rationale: The agent checks the order, states the refund status from ShopKart's records, and raises a ticket. The recipient is asked only for the order number.
legitimate.caller_objective: Resolve the refund query and give the customer a trackable ticket.
stable_facts: The refund was processed four working days ago to the card ending [ACCT_LAST4]; the agent reads these digits out, the recipient does not provide them.
The agent raises ticket [TICKET_ID] and says the bank may take a few more days.
The agent mentions a bank reference number visible on the order page that the recipient can quote to their bank.

agent tells the recipient the ticket is visible in the app's Help section when suspicious.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud agent may press, reassure, or ask for the OTP that follows the card details (same card-payment mechanism). They must not switch to remote-access apps, QR codes, or collect requests. The legitimate agent must not ask for card number, expiry, CVV, PIN, OTP, or any payment.

must_preserve: refund and card wording in both
full card details plus CVV request in _F
ticket and last-four digits read by the agent in _L

ambiguities: In reality the source of the number is the key risk factor, but it is kept private here so the text cannot be labelled from the recipient's words. A variant where the recipient says "I found you on the internet" is not used.
Both agents know the order and amount once the recipient gives the order number; knowledge is not a cue.
Verification" is said in both cases.

evidence_references.claim: Contact numbers found on search engines may be fraudulent (C07)
Genuine entities never ask for card details, CVV, or OTP (C01)
E-commerce platforms must display official customer-care and grievance contacts on the platform (CE11)
Refund scams via fake customer-care numbers ask for OTPs or bank details (CE22)
